newsitem.title: FRANCE: Explosion in Algiers cinema injures five.
newsitem.headline: Explosion in Algiers cinema injures five.

text.p: An explosion in a cinema in the centre of the Algerian capital Algiers injured five people, two of them seriously, on Saturday, the official Algerian news agency APS reported.
Quoting the Algerian security forces, APS said the explosion took place at 4 p.m. (1500 GMT) in a cinema called Casino, injuring five Algerians.
It did not give other details or say whether the explosion was caused by a bomb. APS, referring to the injured people, said this was "a preliminary report".
Algerian newspapers earlier reported more killings and two car bombs in the final days of the country's parliamentary election campaign.
A car bomb exploded in downtown Chlef city, 150 km (100 miles) west of Algiers, on Thursday damaging a bank and shops, said El Watan newspaper.
Al Khabar said another car bomb went off by a car market in Boumerdes region, east of Algiers. No casualties were reported in either bombing.

Moslem guerrillas stormed Fizane mountain hamlet in the coastal province of Tipaza, 60 km (40 miles) southwest of Algiers, late on Thursday killing 14 people, according to the Arabic- language daily Al Khabar. The dead included four elderly men, two women and two pro-government armed villagers, it said.
About 60,000 people have died in Algeria's violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which FIS had taken a commanding lead.
